body: AI agents depend on repeated decisions to accomplish tasks, with large language models (LLMs) commonly serving as their core decision makers. The recent emergence of Jev offers an opportunity to make these decisions faster and at lower cost. However, it remains unclear whether such local savings can be translated into efficient and reliable task completion. In this paper, we investigate this efficiency transfer across five agents in two representative application settings, embodied tasks in ALFWorld and mobile app use in AndroidWorld. Across 4,500 task executions, we jointly evaluate task effectiveness, decision-level and task-level resource use, and execution behavior. Experimental results show that Jev integration substantially reduces decision cost and latency across all five agents, with task-level gains varying by workflow. Task success remains close to baseline levels on ALFWorld and declines more substantially in two mobile agents. Auxiliary reasoning and additional interactions absorb decision savings, while failed recovery and premature completion limit successful delivery. Mean cost per successful outcome increases in one agent even as spending per attempt falls. These findings highlight the importance of preserving progress, supporting recovery, and verifying completion when integrating efficient decision models into agent workflows. Their practical value should be assessed through successful task delivery, recovery behavior, and resources per delivered outcome.
summaryZh: 该研究实证研究了Jev技术在AI代理工作流中的应用效果。Jev能够显著降低决策成本和延迟，但在ALFWorld和AndroidWorld等应用场景中，其对整体任务成功率的影响并不总是积极的。研究发现，辅助推理、额外交互以及失败的恢复机制会消耗决策节省的资源，有时甚至导致每成功一次的成本增加。这表明在将Jev等高效决策模型集成到代理工作流时，必须关注任务的成功交付、恢复行为以及单位成功产出的资源消耗。
